title: Choroidal Neovascularization (CNV): The Resident's Masterclass
summary: Choroidal Neovascularization (CNV) involves the proliferation of abnormal blood vessels from the choriocapillaris through Bruch's membrane. This masterclass covers the pathophysiology, multimodal imaging, and the evolving landscape of anti-VEGF therapies.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: CNV is the growth of new, fragile blood vessels from the choriocapillaris through defects in Bruch’s membrane into the sub-RPE or sub-retinal space. Pathogenesis is driven by an imbalance between pro-angiogenic factors (VEGF, bFGF) and anti-angiogenic factors (PEDF, Angiostatin). Chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, and hypoxia (HIF-1α) are key triggers in conditions like AMD.

branches: Type 1: Sub-RPE (Occult on FFA, most common in AMD)
Type 2: Sub-retinal (Classic on FFA, above RPE)
Type 3: RAP (Retinal Angiomatous Proliferation - originates from retina)
Type 4: Mixed (Components of both Type 1 and 2)
Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy (PCV): Variant with aneurysmal dilations

content.explanation: Causes of CNV: C: Choroidal Rupture, H: Histoplasmosis (POHS), A: Angioid Streaks, M: Myopia (Pathologic), P: Post-inflammatory/PIC, S: Senile (AMD).

sections.title: Clinical Features & Symptoms
content: Subretinal fluid or hemorrhage on fundoscopy

rows: Polyps on ICG; Notch on OCT

sections.title: OCT Biomarkers of Activity
content: Subretinal Fluid (SRF) - Hyporeflective space below retina
Foveal Tubulations - Sign of chronic degeneration

sections.title: Management Protocols
content: 3. Treat-and-Extend (T&E): Extend interval by 1-2 weeks if dry
4. Pro Re Nata (PRN): Inject only when fluid recurs
5. Fixed Interval: Injection every 4-8 weeks regardless of fluid

sections.title: Red Flags & Emergency Signs
content: RPE Rip (Tear) - sudden vision drop during treatment

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Trials
content: MARINA/ANCHOR: Established Ranibizumab superiority over PDT/Sham.
CATT: Bevacizumab is non-inferior to Ranibizumab.
VIEW 1/2: Aflibercept q8w equal to Ranibizumab q4w.
TENAYA/LUCERNE: Faricimab durability up to 16 weeks.
FLUID Study: Tolerate some SRF vs zero-tolerance (T&E).

sections.title: Surgical & Alternative Options
content: Photodynamic Therapy (PDT) - Vertoporfin for PCV or refractory CNV
Susvimo (Port Delivery System) - Continuous Ranibizumab release

sections.title: Clinical Pearls
content: Always check for a 'double-layer sign' on OCT, which may indicate Type 1 CNV or PCV.
Type 2 CNV is more common in inflammatory conditions like PIC or myopia.
Myopic CNV requires fewer injections (often 1-3) compared to AMD.
Persistent Sub-Retinal Fluid (SRF) may sometimes be tolerated if the macula is stable, but IRF must always be treated.
The presence of 'SHRM' is a high-risk factor for poor visual outcome and fibrosis.

sections.title: Complications & Prognosis
content: Geographic Atrophy (can develop during Anti-VEGF therapy)
RPE Tear (Highest risk in large PEDs)
